title: NC circuits have tree representations
statement: Let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings. If $L$ is recognized by a family of well-formed Boolean circuits with fan-in at most two, polynomial size, and depth at most $b(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)$ on inputs of length $n$ for some natural number $b$, then $L$ is recognized by a family of Boolean circuit trees with maximum fan-in at most two, polynomial size, and depth at most $b'(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)$ for some natural number $b'$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is in $\mathrm{NC}^1$ (fan-in at most two, polynomial size, and polylogarithmic depth with exponent one)
